issue.body:
I realized that when a endpoint is not async, it is executed in another python thread:

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse
from starlette.routing import Route
import threading

def startup_task():
    print("startup ", threading.get_ident())

def homepage(request):
    print("homepage", threading.get_ident())
    return JSONResponse({'hello': 'world'})

app = Starlette(
    routes=[Route('/', homepage)],
    on_startup=[startup_task],
)
```
```bash
$ uvicorn example:app
INFO:     Started server process [211944]
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
INFO:     Waiting for application startup.
startup  140630902069056
INFO:     Application startup complete.
homepage 140630840559360
INFO:     127.0.0.1:57170 - "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```
I see no mention of this in the documentation. Maybe it worth having a word on this?

For some reasons I have to work with some legacy endpoints. They are not async, and I cannot change this easily. They use [threading local data](https://docs.python.org/3/library/threading.html#threading.local) that are initialized the same time the application is launched.

```python
def startup_task():
    initialize_my_thread_data()

def homepage(request):
    read_my_thread_data()
    return JSONResponse({'hello': 'world'})

app = Starlette(
    routes=[Route('/', homepage)],
    on_startup=[startup_task],
)
```

In this situation, the endpoint cannot access the data initialized earlier. I would love a `on_thread_startup` event that could handle my thread data initializations.

What do you think?
issue.title: on_thread_startup event
